Commentary.Commentary: So! Can Ireland take an unassailable 2-1 lead in the series? They do not have a great asking rate and it is all about one batsman batting till the end. Join us back in a while for the run chase.

Ireland might be looking at this as a missed opportunity with Afghanistan tottering at 81/6. But they can also view it as the pitch getting better to bat on. James Cameron Dow was the surprise package today, finishing with a 3-fer. McBrine was decent too, being economical with the new ball.

Like the previous game, here too, the visitors had the Afghans in disarray. The hosts were 81/6 but then, a 50-run stand for the 7th wicket followed by a mammoth 86-run partnership for the 8th, steered the Afghans out of troubled waters. Mohammad Nabi was the catalyst in both the partnerships, finishing with a wonderful 64 from 85 balls. And what about Rashid? He is no longer just a bowler. He can bat too! His quickfire 52 from 58 ensured that Afghanistan took this innings into the 50th over.

224 is the target for Ireland then. A little less than the one a couple of days ago. The mantra of winning the toss and putting Afghanistan to bat first seems to be working. Now, to see whether the Irish can bat decently in the run chase.

OUT! Run out! The direct hit has found Afghan short! Big moment in the game. Out of nowhere, Ireland have struck gold. A length ball outside off, Nabi pushed this towards point and set off for a single. Afghan responded but so did George Dockrell. He came running in from cover as the fielder from point dived to his right, parrying it towards him. Meanwhile, both the batsmen were ball-watching. Nabi stopped while Afghan stopped on the run. Then, when the ball was not stopped cleanly, both started to run. Dockrell swooped onto it, took an aim at the striker's end and whoosh! Bull's eye! Asghar landed awkwardly on the ground and clutched his right shoulder. It was referred upstairs and replays confirmed the worst. The 50-run stand is broken.
Run out chance! Is Asghar gone? Seems like it. The Irish are celebrating...

Hello and welcome to the 4th ODI between Afghanistan and Ireland at Dehradun. The visitors have bounced back and would look to maintain their confidence to win this match and put pressure on the hosts. It was Andy Balbirnie's century which sealed the match for them in the last game. On the other hand, Afghanistan would look to improve their batting and will want Hazratullah Zazai and Mohammad Shahzad to fire. Last match it was their skipper Asghar Afghan who played a good knock. The pitch will offer help for the spinners. Stay tuned for the toss.
